title: Ensure Authentication is configured
description: This setting ensures that all clients, users, servers are required to authenticate before being granted access to the MongoDB database. Authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a client. When access control, i.e. authorization, is enabled, MongoDB requires all clients to authenticate themselves in order to determine their access. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure Authentication is configured

remediation.command: Create a user administrator first (use admin; db.createUser({user: '<admin>', pwd: passwordPrompt(), roles: [{role: 'userAdminAnyDatabase', db: 'admin'}]})), then set 'security: authorization: enabled' in /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod.

title: Ensure mongod does not listen on all interfaces
description: bindIp 0.0.0.0 or bindIpAll exposes the database on every network interface; bind only to localhost and required private addresses. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB Benchmark - Network Exposure / Bind Address (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: Set net.bindIp to 127.0.0.1 plus the specific private addresses required (remove bindIpAll), then restart mongod

title: Ensure that MongoDB does not bypass authentication via the localhost exception
description: MongoDB should not be set to bypass authentication via the localhost exception. The localhost exception allows the user to enable authorization before creating the first user in the system. When active, the localhost exception allows all connections from the localhost interface to have full access to that instance. The exception applies only when there are no users created in the MongoDB instance. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). The localhost exception is enabled by default, so the setting must be present and false.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure that MongoDB does not bypass authentication via the localhost exception

remediation.guidance: Add 'setParameter: {enableLocalhostAuthBypass: false}' to /etc/mongod.conf (or start mongod with --setParameter enableLocalhostAuthBypass=0) and restart mongod.

title: Ensure authentication is enabled in the sharded cluster
description: Authentication is enabled in a sharded cluster when the certificate or key files are created and configured for all components. This ensures that every client that accesses the cluster must provide credentials, to include MongoDB instances that access each other within the cluster. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). The benchmark requires x.509 membership authentication (keyFile is accepted only for development); applies to sharded clusters and replica sets.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 2.3 Ensure authentication is enabled in the sharded cluster

remediation.command: On every member configure net.tls (mode: requireTLS, certificateKeyFile, CAFile, clusterFile) and security.clusterAuthMode: x509, then perform a rolling restart.

title: Ensure least privilege for database accounts
description: MongoDB grants access to data and commands through "role-based" approach, MongoDB is shipped with built-in roles that provide the different levels of access commonly needed in a database system. In addition, you can create custom-roles.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure least privilege for database accounts

audit.command: In mongosh run db.getSiblingDB("admin").system.users.find({"roles.role": {$in: ["dbOwner", "userAdmin", "userAdminAnyDatabase"]}, "roles.db": "admin"}, {user: 1, roles: 1}). Any account returned holds a built-in dbOwner/userAdmin/userAdminAnyDatabase role scoped to the admin database and must be justified or dropped.

remediation.command: If any accounts were listed with built in-roles: dbOwner userAdmin userAdminAnyDatabase in "admin" database role then drop them.

title: Ensure that MongoDB is run using a non-privileged, dedicated service account
description: The MongoDB service should not be run using a privileged account such as 'root' because this unnecessarily exposes the operating system to high risk. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when every running mongod/mongos process runs as a non-root account (FAIL when none are running).
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure that MongoDB is run using a non-privileged, dedicated service account

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user=,comm= 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '$2 == "mongod" || $2 == "mongos" {n++; if ($1 == "root") r++} END {if (n == 0) print "not running"; else if (r > 0) print "root"; else print "compliant"}'

remediation.command: Create a dedicated mongodb system account, make the data, keyfile and TLS key files readable only by it, set User=mongodb in the service unit and restart mongod.

title: Review Superuser/Admin Roles
description: Roles provide several advantages that make it easier to manage privileges in a database system. Security administrators can control access to their databases in a way that mirrors the structure of their organizations (they can create roles in the database that map directly to the job functions in their organizations). The assignment of privileges is simplified.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.5 Review Superuser/Admin Roles

audit.command: In mongosh run db.runCommand({rolesInfo: 1, showBuiltinRoles: true}) and db.getSiblingDB("admin").system.users.find({"roles.role": {$in: ["root", "dbOwner", "userAdmin", "userAdminAnyDatabase", "readWriteAnyDatabase", "dbAdminAnyDatabase", "clusterAdmin", "hostManager", "restore"]}}, {user: 1, roles: 1}). Confirm each holder of a superuser/admin role is approved; revoke the rest with db.revokeRolesFromUser().

remediation.command: To remove a user from one or more roles on the current database. use \<dbName\> db.revokeRolesFromUser( "\<username\>", [ \<roles\> ])

title: Ensure Weak Protocols are Disabled
description: Servers can be configured to disable specific TLS/SSL protocol versions which may be vulnerable to exploitation and/or lack features which improve the level of security as provided by newer versions of the protocol. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.2 Ensure Weak Protocols are Disabled

remediation.command: Set net.tls.disabledProtocols: TLS1_0,TLS1_1 in /etc/mongod.conf (or start with --tlsDisabledProtocols TLS1_0,TLS1_1) and restart mongod.

title: Ensure Encryption of Data in Transit TLS or SSL (Transport Encryption)
description: Use TLS or SSL to protect all incoming and outgoing connections. This should include using TLS or SSL to encrypt communication between the mongod and mongos components of a MongoDB client as well as between all applications and MongoDB. MongoDB supports TLS/SSL (Transport Layer Security/Secure Sockets Layer) to encrypt all of MongoDB's network traffic. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.3 Ensure Encryption of Data in Transit TLS or SSL (Transport Encryption)

remediation.command: Set net.tls.mode: requireTLS with net.tls.certificateKeyFile and net.tls.CAFile in /etc/mongod.conf, update clients to use TLS, then restart mongod.

title: Ensure that system activity is audited
description: Track access and changes to database configurations and data. MongoDB Enterprise includes a system auditing facility that can record system events (e.g. user operations, connection events) on a MongoDB instance. These audit records permit forensic analysis and allow administrators to verify proper controls. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). Auditing requires MongoDB Enterprise or Percona Server for MongoDB.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure that system activity is audited

remediation.command: Add 'auditLog: {destination: file, format: JSON, path: /var/log/mongodb/auditLog.json}' (or destination: syslog) to /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod.

title: Ensure appropriate key file permissions are set
description: In the Shared Cluster, the certificate or keyfile is utilized for authentications. Implementing proper file permissions on the certificate or keyfile will prevent unauthorized access to it. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). Every keyFile, PEMKeyFile, certificateKeyFile and clusterFile referenced in the config must be mode 600 or stricter (a referenced file that cannot be read also fails).
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 7.1 Ensure appropriate key file permissions are set

audit.command: [ -r /etc/mongod.conf ] || exit 1; bad=0; for f in $(awk '/^[[:space:]]*(keyFile|PEMKeyFile|certificateKeyFile|clusterFile):/ {v=$2; gsub(/["\047]/, "", v); print v}' /etc/mongod.conf); do p=$(stat -c %a "$f" 2>/dev/null) || { bad=1; continue; }; [ $((0$p & 077)) -eq 0 ] || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.guidance: chmod 600 <keyfile/PEM key> and chown mongodb:mongodb <keyfile/PEM key> for every key file referenced in /etc/mongod.conf.

title: Ensure appropriate database file permissions are set
description: MongoDB database files need to be protected using file permissions. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). storage.dbPath (default /var/lib/mongodb) must be 770 or stricter, with no access for other users.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 7.2 Ensure appropriate database file permissions are set

audit.command: [ -r /etc/mongod.conf ] || exit 1; d=$(awk '/^[[:space:]]*dbPath:/ {v=$2; gsub(/["\047]/, "", v); print v}' /etc/mongod.conf); d=${d:-/var/lib/mongodb}; p=$(stat -c %a "$d" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ $((0$p & 007)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "mode $p"; fi

title: Ensure /etc/mongod.conf is not writable by group or readable by others
description: The configuration file can reference key files and TLS settings; it should be mode 640 or stricter. SKIP when the file does not exist.
reference: CIS MongoDB Benchmark - File Permissions / Configuration File (verify section number for your release)

audit.command: p=$(stat -c %a /etc/mongod.conf 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; if [ $((0$p & 037)) -eq 0 ]; then echo compliant; else echo "mode $p"; fi

remediation.command: chmod 640 /etc/mongod.conf

title: Ensure system activity is logged to a file or syslog
description: systemLog.destination file or syslog keeps server logs persistently instead of only on stdout. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB Benchmark - Audit Logging / System Log (verify section number for your release)

remediation.command: Set systemLog.destination: file and systemLog.path: /var/log/mongodb/mongod.log in /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod

title: Ensure the appropriate MongoDB software version/patches are installed
description: The MongoDB installation version, along with the patch level, should be the most recent that is compatible with the organization's operational needs. In addition, regularly view latest minor security patch updates for security vulnerability fixes (CVE Related) from MongoDB website: https://www.mongodb.com/alerts
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 1.1 Ensure the appropriate MongoDB software version/patches are installed

audit.command: Run mongod --version (Windows: mongod.exe --version) and db.version() in mongosh. Compare the running release with the MongoDB supported-versions and security-advisory pages; the version must be supported and carry the latest patch release your organisation has approved.

remediation.command: Upgrade to the latest version of the MongoDB software: 1. Backup the data set. 2. Download the binaries for the latest MongoDB revision from the MongoDB Download Page and store the binaries in a temporary location. The binaries download as compressed files that extract to the directory structure used by the MongoDB installation. 3. Shutdown the MongoDB instance. 4. Replace the existing MongoDB binaries with the downloaded binaries. 5.

title: Ensure that role-based access control is enabled and configured appropriately
description: Role-based access control (RBAC) is a method of regulating access to resources based on the roles of individual users within an enterprise. A user is granted one or more roles that determine the user's access to database resources and operations. Outside of role assignments, the user has no access to the system. MongoDB can use RBAC to govern access to MongoDB systems.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure that role-based access control is enabled and configured appropriately

audit.command: Connect with mongosh as the user administrator and list users and roles (db.getUsers(), db.getRoles({showPrivileges: true}) in each database). Verify every user is assigned only the roles it needs and that privileges are granted through roles rather than individually.

remediation.command: 1. Establish roles for MongoDB. 2. Assign the appropriate privileges to each role. 3. Assign the appropriate users to each role. 4. Remove any individual privileges assigned to users that are now addressed by the roles. 5. See the reference below for more Information.

title: Ensure that each role for each MongoDB database is needed and grants only the necessary privileges
description: Reviewing all roles periodically and eliminating unneeded roles as well as unneeded privileges from necessary roles helps minimize the privileges that each user has.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure that each role for each MongoDB database is needed and grants only the necessary privileges

audit.command: Perform the following command to view all roles on the database on which the command runs, including both built-in and user-defined roles, as well as the privileges granted by each role. Ensure that only necessary roles are listed and only the necessary privileges are listed for each role. db.runCommand( { rolesInfo: 1, showPrivileges: true, showBuiltinRoles: true } )

remediation.command: To revoke specified privileges from the user-defined role on the database where the command is run. The revokePrivilegesFromRole command has the following syntax: { revokePrivilegesFromRole: "\<role\>", privileges:  [  { resource: { \<resource\> }, actions: [ "\<action\>", ... ] },  ...  ], }

title: Ensure legacy TLS protocols are disabled
description: Only modern TLS protocols should be enabled in MongoDB for all client connections and upstream connections. Removing legacy TLS and SSL protocols (SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0 and 1.1), and enabling emerging and stable TLS protocols (TLS 1.2, and TLS 1.3), ensures users are able to take advantage of strong security capabilities and protects them from insecure legacy protocols. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.1 Ensure legacy TLS protocols are disabled

remediation.command: Add 'disabledProtocols: TLS1_0,TLS1_1' under net.tls in /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod/mongos.

title: Ensure Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) is enabled
description: The Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) is a computer security standard used to certify software modules and libraries that encrypt and decrypt data securely. You can configure MongoDB to run with a FIPS 140-2 certified library for OpenSSL. FIPS is a property of the encryption system and not the access control system. However, the environment requires FIPS compliant encryption and access control. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). FIPS mode requires MongoDB Enterprise and a FIPS-validated OpenSSL.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.4 Ensure Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) is enabled

remediation.command: Use FIPS-compliant certificates, set net.tls.FIPSMode: true in /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod; confirm 'FIPS 140-2 mode activated' in the log.

title: Ensure Encryption of Data at Rest
description: Encryption of data at rest must be enabled to ensure compliance with security and privacy standards including HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and FERPA. Encryption at rest, when used in conjunction with transport encryption and good security policies that protect relevant accounts, passwords, and encryption keys. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). Requires MongoDB Enterprise (encrypted WiredTiger storage engine); also confirm a KMIP server or encryptionKeyFile holds the master key and that keys are rotated.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 4.5 Ensure Encryption of Data at Rest

remediation.command: Configure security.enableEncryption: true with security.kmip.* (recommended) or security.encryptionKeyFile, then resync each member so its data files are rewritten encrypted; rotate keys per policy.

title: Ensure that audit filters are configured properly
description: MongoDB Enterprise supports auditing of various operations. When enabled, the audit facility, by default, records all auditable operations as detailed in Audit Event Actions, Details, and Results. To specify which events to record, the audit feature includes the - -auditFilter option. This check is only for Enterprise editions.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.2 Ensure that audit filters are configured properly

audit.command: To verify that audit filters are configured on MongoDB as per the organization's requirements, run the following command: On Ubuntu: cat /etc/mongod.conf |grep -A10 "auditLog" | grep "filter" On Windows: type mongod.conf | findstr -A10 "auditLog" | findstr "filter"

remediation.command: Set the audit filters based on the organization's requirements.

title: Ensure that server-side scripting is disabled if not needed
description: MongoDB supports the execution of JavaScript code for certain server-side operations: mapReduce, group, $where, $accumulator, and $function aggregation operations that allow users to define custom aggregation expressions. If you do not use these operations, server-side scripting should be disabled. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). Treat a FAIL as an accepted exception only where server-side JavaScript ($where, mapReduce, $function, $accumulator) is required.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 6.3 Ensure that server-side scripting is disabled if not needed

remediation.guidance: If server-side scripting is not required set security.javascriptEnabled: false in /etc/mongod.conf (or start mongod/mongos with --noscripting) and restart.

title: Ensure client data is redacted from logs
description: security.redactClientLogData: true keeps document contents out of diagnostic logs (MongoDB Enterprise). Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB Benchmark - Data Encryption / Log Redaction (verify section number for your release)

remediation.guidance: Set security.redactClientLogData: true in /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod

title: Ensure that logging captures as much information as possible
description: The SystemLog.quiet option stops logging of information such as: - connection events - authentication events - replication sync activities - evidence of some potentially impactful commands being run (eg: drop, dropIndexes, validate) This information should be logged whenever possible. This check is only for Enterprise editions. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). Passes when systemLog.quiet is absent or false.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.3 Ensure that logging captures as much information as possible

remediation.guidance: Set systemLog.quiet: false (or remove the quiet setting) in /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod.

title: Ensure that new entries are appended to the end of the log file
description: By default, new log entries will overwrite old entries after a restart of the mongod or Mongols service. Enabling the systemLog.logAppend setting causes new entries to be appended to the end of the log file rather than overwriting the existing content of the log when the mongos or mongod instance restarts. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist).
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 5.4 Ensure that new entries are appended to the end of the log file

remediation.guidance: Set systemLog.logAppend: true in /etc/mongod.conf and restart mongod.

title: Ensure that MongoDB uses a non-default port
description: Changing the default port used by MongoDB makes it harder for attackers to find the database and target it. Checks the YAML config file /etc/mongod.conf (SKIP when it does not exist). A missing net.port means the default 27017 is used and fails.
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 6.1 Ensure that MongoDB uses a non-default port

audit.command: [ -r /etc/mongod.conf ] || exit 1; awk '/^[[:space:]]*port:/ {v=$2; gsub(/["\047]/, "", v); p=v} END {print (p != "" && p != "27017") ? "compliant" : "default port"}' /etc/mongod.conf

remediation.command: Set net.port to an organisation-defined port other than 27017 in /etc/mongod.conf, update firewall rules and client connection strings, then restart mongod.

title: Ensure that operating system resource limits are set for MongoDB
description: Operating systems provide ways to limit and control the usage of system resources such as threads, files, and network connections on a per-process and per-user basis
reference: CIS MongoDB 8 Benchmark v2.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure that operating system resource limits are set for MongoDB

audit.command: To verify the resource limits set for MongoDB, run the following commands. Extract the process ID for MongoDB: ps -ef | grep mongod View the limits associated with that process number: cat /proc/1322/limits

remediation.command: Every deployment may have unique requirements and settings. Recommended thresholds and settings are particularly important for MongoDB deployments: - f (file size): unlimited - t (cpu time): unlimited - v (virtual memory): unlimited [1] - n (open files): 64000 - m (memory size): unlimited [1] [2] - u (processes/threads): 64000 Restart the mongod and mongos instances after changing the ulimit settings to ensure that the changes take effect.
